decisions.question: The relationship taxonomy carries ten kinds. Can HCL express a call graph, a class hierarchy, or object construction?
decisions.resolution:
SUPERSEDED 2026-10-09: this ruling was refuted by measurement in three independent ways, and is kept as the record because a wrong ruling that is quietly deleted cannot warn anyone. (1) It ruled `calls`/`overrides` NOT APPLICABLE while the analyzer emits both — src/ast/real-hcl-analyzer.ts:485 (Overrides) and :528 (Calls) — and this lane's own committed fixtures assert them: validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/declared-function-call.expectation.json expects 3 `calls` edges and validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/override-target-not-reference.expectation.json expects 4 `overrides` edges. A verdict contradicted by the code and the fixtures is a verdict produced by an instrument nobody read. (2) Its cited adjudication artefact, `fixtures/hcl/out/calls-feasibility.json`, DOES NOT EXIST on this laptop, and the instrument that wrote it imports a hardcoded `$HOME/backbencher-brain/src/ast/engine` — a path that does not exist here (the repo is $HOME/mcp/backbencher-brain). A ruling that rests on a missing artifact is not a ruling. (3) Its `extends` half was wrong for a different reason: it probed node types and block types and never the attribute-key vocabulary, and the whole-corpus census found 44 docker-bake `inherits` sites in 8 files whose 53 named parents all resolve to `target` blocks declared in the same file. The measured replacement is HCL-D1a (extends/implements/instantiates) and HCL-D9 (calls/overrides).

[UNION: the version from the other side read — NOT APPLICABLE, and each half is measured rather than asserted. `extends`/`implements`/`overrides`: HCL has no type declaration, no base clause and no interface implementation among the grammar's 64 named node types, so the kinds are not merely unused but inexpressible. `instantiates`: HCL builds values with `object()`/`list()`, never instances of a declared type. `calls`: 12,977 `function_call` nodes over 144 distinct callees in 9,079 files, and NOT ONE callee resolves to a symbol the project declares, because the grammar provides no syntax for declaring one; the 5 that appear to match are provable name collisions (Terraform core functions `length`, `file`, `timestamp`, `lower`, and the type keyword `object` beside a declared `output "object"`). Every `calls` edge would therefore dangle, which is the shape java and groovy suppress with explicit builtin filters. The reference read INSIDE a call is still published. ENFORCED, not merely stated: run-fixtures.ts's UNIVERSAL_FORBIDDEN_RELATIONSHIPS for hcl refuses extends/implements into the reference roots var/local/module/data, and the hcl/builtin-vs-project-reference fixture forbids a `calls` edge to toset/merge/lookup. Adjudication: fixtures/hcl/out/calls-feasibility.json.]

decisions.resolution: RULED per type, over the CENSUS corpus (9,329 git-tracked .tf/.tfvars/.hcl/.tofu files, 16 repositories, 1,645,992 named nodes — the lane's own walk over $HOME/fixtures/repositories; THE ARM POPULATION IS 11,139 admitted (the gate's own line — script/m14/incoming-gate.ts over root $PWD/.corpus = $HOME/mcp/backbencher-brain/.corpus, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; 38 width-300 slices, contiguous [0, 11,139), CLOSURE EXACT 307,748) and IS the declaration's (validation/m14/instruments/hcl/incoming-declaration.json, derived at HEAD; committed at ba88f2959/e68b41ca7). Instrument: validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/tools/construct-census.mts; artefact: validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/construct-census.current.json. Control: 49 planted keywords were seen as block types AND as attribute keys, and the production path emitted the planted `calls`/`overrides`/`contains` edges, so a corpus zero below is a zero the probe could have seen through. `extends` = a GAP UNTIL HCL-D10: the HCL container grammar has no inheritance production, but the language as used CAN express inheritance — `inherits = ["base"]` inside a docker-bake `target` block names other declarations — and the census measured 44 such sites in 8 files naming 53 parents, 53/53 resolving to a `target` declared in the same file and 0 unresolved. A construct that exists and occurs cannot be excluded, so the type stayed IN the denominator as an unimplemented gap until HCL-D10 emitted it (53 edges, 53/53 binding). This is also the measurement that corrected the lane's own earlier instrument-A reading, which enumerated block types and node types but never the attribute-key vocabulary. `implements` = GRAMMAR-ABSENCE: 0 of 18 declaration-shaped node types are produced by the pinned grammar, and 0 of the corpus's 455 distinct block types and 0 of its 5,311 attribute keys name an interface, protocol, trait, impl or satisfies construct; the single candidate keyword, `protocol`, has 162 sites in 50 files and every captured site is DATA (an ALB/security-group/enos network protocol or a matrix value), not contract satisfaction. Leaves the denominator. `instantiates` = ZERO-SITES, and deliberately NOT emitted: the language can express an instantiation (`resource "T" "n" {}`), so a grammar inventory cannot settle it, and the census measured 3,932 resource/data blocks over 444 distinct type labels with 0 of those labels declared as an address anywhere in the corpus (a provider type is declared by a provider binary, in no repository); the 2 `new` attribute-key sites are data attributes in terraform test fixtures. STAYS IN the denominator. Falsifier for the extends half: an `inherits` value that resolves to no `target` in the same file. Falsifier for the instantiates half: a corpus file declaring a named type that a resource/data block instantiates.

decisions.node_type: calls and overrides — the two types the handover ruled inapplicable and the analyzer emits
decisions.question: The handover listed `calls` and `overrides` as missing on prose grounds. Do they exist in HCL, and does the analyzer emit them?
decisions.resolution: RULED, and both are IMPLEMENTED and pinned. `calls`: the ecosystem layers a declaration on top of the container grammar — docker-bake spells it `function "name" { … }` — and the census found exactly 1 such declaration (docker/docker-bake.hcl, `function "bindir"`) among 12,988 `function_call` nodes over 148 distinct callees; the analyzer emits a `calls` edge only where the SAME FILE declares the callee, so every emitted edge resolves and the 12,988 global/provider calls publish no edge while the reference read inside them is still published. `overrides`: Terraform's test framework spells it `override_resource`/`override_data`/`override_module`; the census counted 71 blocks of those three kinds in 33 files with 68 carrying a `target` (72 blocks named override* in total — the extra one is a bare `overrides` block in vault/enos/modules/target_ec2_spot_fleet/main.tf that the analyzer does not recognise), and the edge is a RETYPE of the `references` edge the target used to carry, so the graph gains no duplicate. Both are pinned by committed fixtures (declared-function-call, override-target-not-reference, builtin-vs-project-reference). The 120-file terragrunt firing stride reads both SILENT because neither construct occurs in terragrunt; that is a fact about the sample, not about the language.

decisions.node_type: extends — docker-bake target inheritance, emitted from the `inherits` attribute key
decisions.question: HCL-G1 recorded 44 `inherits` sites in 8 files as an open gap: the construct exists and resolves, but no `extends` edge was published. Should the relation be published as `extends`, and does that label overstate a MERGE as inheritance?
decisions.resolution: IMPLEMENTED, with the label's limit measured rather than assumed. src/ast/real-hcl-analyzer.ts reads `inherits` inside a `target` block, collects the string LITERALS (a bare `"x"` or a list; an interpolated template names a computed value and is skipped), and resolves each AFTER the DFS against a `target` declared in the SAME file — docker-bake.hcl's own `binary-cross` inherits `_platforms`, declared BELOW it, so forward-only resolution would drop real inheritance. Each parent becomes `extends` from the child's address to the parent's address (`target.binary -> target._common`), with `hclSite: "inherits"` and `hclInheritedTarget` carrying the spelling at the site; an unresolved parent publishes NOTHING, because a dangling `extends` is worse than a missing one. Emission measured 2026-10-09: 53 edges over the 8 docker-bake files, 53/53 binding to a declaration in the same file, 0 unresolved (`.tmp-hcl/extends-after.mts`); `ontology-coverage-gate.ts hcl --fresh` now reads `extends EMITTED 53 edges` and the type left the FALSIFIED list. Pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/docker-bake-inherits.tf, whose pre-change run is recorded as 11 pass / 1 fail. THE LABEL'S LIMIT, stated: `inherits` is a MERGE, not a subtype derivation — 16 of the 44 inheriting targets re-declare at least one key they also inherit, and 25 of the 53 parent occurrences are abstract bases by docker-bake's leading-underscore convention while the rest are functional targets. `extends` is the house label for exactly this shape (the yaml lane labels `<<: *base` merge-key reuse `extends`), the relation is between DECLARATIONS, it is directional, and a change to the parent does propagate to the child — which is what a consumer following `extends` needs. NOT published, and therefore stated rather than silently dropped: a child's re-declaration of an inherited key is NOT a separate `overrides` edge (16 sites). Falsifier: a corpus file whose `inherits` names a target no file declares would publish nothing and the rule would need re-examination as an unresolvable class.

decisions.node_type: 441 distinct block types across the measured corpus
decisions.question: The corpus contains 441 distinct block types; the analyzer classifies 8 Terraform top-level kinds and calls the rest nested. Is the remainder a gap?
decisions.resolution: RULED, not a gap. The remainder is legitimate in its own DSLs — terragrunt include/dependency/feature, packer source/build, nomad job/task/group, consul/vault/boundary config — and each is a real block in the HCL container grammar, emitted as kind `class` with hclBlockKind `nested`, which is truthful. This lane extracts the HCL CONTAINER grammar; a terragrunt `dependency { config_path = ... }` is a block, and reading it as a cross-file edge would be a guess the grammar does not support. The 8 Terraform top-level kinds carry their own kind (resource/data -> class, variable/output -> variable, module/provider/terraform/locals -> module).

decisions.node_type: Go-template directives read as reference paths (2 occurrences, 1 file)
decisions.question: The corpus differential's only 2 MISSED references are `range.requiredVariables` and `if.requiredVariables`, from terragrunt/test/fixtures/catalog/local-template/.boilerplate/terragrunt.hcl. Defect?
decisions.resolution: RULED, analyzer-is-faithful. That file is a Go text/template that happens to be named `.hcl`; `{{- range .requiredVariables }}` is not HCL, and the grammar parses `{{-` as a binary operation whose operands read as a two-segment path, so the emission is faithful to the bytes. Suppressing it would mean keying on the template words if/range/with/define, which are also legal HCL identifier bases — the rule would cost more than the 2 occurrences in 9,079 files it removes. Recorded rather than hidden: this is the entire measured recall residual, 0.000069.

decisions.node_type: swallow class — a block the grammar never produces under template damage (2 files)
decisions.question: boundary/internal/cmd/commands/config/fixtures/config_ext_decrypt.hcl holds a real `kms "aead" { … }` after two Go-template `{{decrypt(…)}}` lines, and the analyzer emits 1 symbol where minimal reconstruction yields 4. Is a declaration being swallowed?
decisions.resolution: RULED, with the loss measured rather than asserted. The grammar decomposes the block into identifier + literal_value + an expression/collection_value/object and emits NO `block` node at all, so a block-driven walker has nothing to find; the same shape occurs in 2 of 9,079 files (22 ppm). Proven by minimal reconstruction through parseFile — the method the lane formula prescribes: deleting the two template lines recovers kms.aead plus purpose and aead_type, 4 symbols against 1. No heuristic recovery was added: a rule keyed on this damaged shape is a confidence-<1 guess over 2 files, which costs more in false-edge risk than it recovers. The REACHABLE form of the class — a real `block` node inside an ERROR region — is handled: the walker descends through ERROR nodes, which is why the 244 corpus ERROR files still yield 135,645 symbols.

decisions.node_type: duplicate attribute key inside one block (21 corpus identities)
decisions.question: After sibling disambiguation 21 (scope,name) pairs still repeat, all ATTRIBUTE keys rather than blocks: `terraform.backend.local|path` on lines 3 and 4, `duplicate|foo` in a file named duplicate.tfvars, `import|id`, `storage.raft|retry_join` eight times. Disambiguate them too?
decisions.resolution: RULED, deliberately NOT disambiguated. A repeated key in one block is rejected by Terraform outright ('Attribute redefined'), so the collision is inherited from invalid input, and inventing a second identity for it would misrepresent a file that does not exist in the language. BLOCKS are disambiguated — many legitimately repeat, which is what HCL-D2's 441 types are made of — because a repeated block is legal. Every one of the 21 sits in a file whose name or path declares the intent: invalid-backend-configuration/repeated-attr, duplicate.tfvars, agent_config_duplicate_keys.hcl, raft_retry_join_attr.hcl.

decisions.question: The grammar makes the whole enclosing block one ERROR node for a quoted attribute key, so the block's declarations are lost. Parse gap?
decisions.resolution: RULED, correct per specification. HCL2's native syntax defines Attribute as `Identifier "=" Expression`, so a quoted key is not the native spelling; the JSON-ish spelling is a different file format that gets its own extension. Measured: nomad/command/agent/testdata/sample1/sample2.hcl (`"advertise" = {…}`) is one of the 13 legitimately symbol-free corpus files. No recovery attempted — the input is not HCL.

decisions.node_type: ERROR — tree-sitter's runtime error node (not a grammar type)
decisions.question: `ERROR` is observed on 244 corpus files but is declared by no node type in the grammar, so where does it belong in a completeness classification whose rule is 'every node type the wasm produces is in exactly one bucket'?
decisions.resolution: RULED, and deliberately kept OUT of all three buckets. The completeness gate's own rule 2 makes a row the wasm does not produce a stale row, and `ERROR` is produced by the parser at runtime, not declared by the grammar, so it has no stable place in a grammar-type census. What IS true about it is recorded where it can be checked: the analyzer emits nothing FOR an ERROR node and deliberately DESCENDS THROUGH it, which is what keeps a surviving declaration reachable under grammar damage. That descent is the mechanism behind the hcl/negative-syntax-error fixture, it is what yields 135,645 symbols across the 244 damaged corpus files, and the one shape it still cannot reach — a block the grammar never produces at all — is HCL-D4's 2 files in 9,079, measured and ruled.

decisions.node_type: the two reference CLASSES — a project address vs a language builtin
decisions.question: `references` and `uses` are distinct values in the taxonomy and HCL emits both. What decides which one an edge gets, and is the distinction real or cosmetic?
decisions.resolution: REAL, and it was wrong before this wave. The house precedent is real-sql-analyzer.ts:1569 — a target in a GLOBAL namespace is `uses`, a project symbol is `references`. HCL's reference roots divide exactly that way, and the analyzer was publishing BOTH classes as `references`: 2,029 edges (4.6% of all references) whose root is count/each/self/path/terraform, led by path.module (506), each.key (325), each.value (285) and count.index (214). None of those resolve in the index — no file can declare them, since `count.index` exists wherever a `count` argument does. Publishing them as `references` asserted a declaration that does not exist. They are now `uses` with evidenceClass `builtin_qualified` and `hclBuiltin: true`; the 41,882 project addresses keep `references` with `reference_qualified` (41,882 + 2,029 = 43,911, unchanged — nothing added or dropped, only labelled). The class boundary is enforced in BOTH directions, because the two errors are not symmetric: a builtin published as `references` asserts a phantom declaration, and a project address published as `uses` demotes a real declaration out of the reference graph and out of every consumer that follows `references`. The corpus differential therefore checks the LABEL as well as the target and reports `mislabelled: 0`; hcl/builtin-vs-project-reference pins both halves, with the mutants hcl/builtin-published-as-reference and hcl/project-published-as-builtin.

decisions.node_type: part_of — the four extended values, one at a time: `part_of` closed at R3 from terragrunt `include`
decisions.question: Does HCL express a textual/structural file inclusion (a unit whose members are spliced INTO another document), and if so on which rung?
decisions.resolution: IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-28 at R3, with the ladder walked and recorded. R1 (different/newer build): the pinned grammar is the only published tree-sitter-hcl the corpus routes through and every build of it is a CONTAINER grammar — `include` is a plain `block`, not a missing syntax, so a newer build has nothing extra to give; the construct was already expressible. R2 (patch the grammar): unnecessary and therefore not taken — patching is for a construct the grammar mis-lexes or cannot produce, and this one is already a `block` node. R3 (existing node): the rung taken. THE DISCRIMINATOR, measured: Terraform `module { source = … }` is NOT this relation — the module is a separate unit addressed `module.NAME.*`, its configuration is never spliced into the caller's document (the caller passes inputs and reads outputs, both namespaced), so it earns `imports` and no `part_of`. The corpus census measured 2,042 module `source` sites: 940 local-relative + 1 local-absolute (905 of the 940 resolve to a module directory holding HCL), 496 registry-public, 193 vcs-remote, 364 registry-with-subdirectory spelling, 49 non-literal/dynamic, 3 blocks with no source — and no class of it is a textual splice. THE CONSTRUCT THAT IS ONE: terragrunt `include` — terragrunt MERGES the included file's configuration into the child (which is why a root file's remote_state/dependencies are visible in a child), so the included file becomes a part of the including document. Measured on the CENSUS population (9,329 files / 16 repositories — the lane's own walk, the same extension set `tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu` the router table admits. CENSUS (9,329): the lane's own walk — `git ls-files` per checkout under $HOME/fixtures/repositories, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; instrument validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/tools/construct-census.mts + script/m14/hcl-extended-census.ts; parsed=9329/9329 of THAT walk, 16 repositories. THESE ARE CENSUS COUNTS. THE ARM POPULATION IS 11,139 admitted (the gate's own line — script/m14/incoming-gate.ts over root $PWD/.corpus = $HOME/mcp/backbencher-brain/.corpus, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; 38 width-300 slices, contiguous [0, 11,139), CLOSURE EXACT 307,748) and IS the declaration's (validation/m14/instruments/hcl/incoming-declaration.json, derived at HEAD; committed at ba88f2959/e68b41ca7). NO CONSTRUCT COUNT IN THIS SPEC WAS MEASURED ON IT: the two are different populations and a count from one is never quoted as the other's.): 287 `include` blocks, 0 with no `path` attribute, 22 with a LITERAL path (all 22 naming a file inside the admitted population — the resolvable class), 265 COMPUTED (`find_in_parent_folders(...)` is the canonical terragrunt spelling; an interpolated template is the same fact in another spelling — a value computed at runtime names no file a parse can know, so these publish NOTHING rather than a guessed path). The production path emits exactly 22 `part_of` edges over 17 files, 22/22 literal sites — the census's own control, exact (script/m14/hcl-extended-census.ts, artefact validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/extended-census.current.json). THE EDGE: source = the including document's root-module symbol; target = the INCLUDED file's root-module symbol (its file stem — the same spelling documentName() gives every HCL file), never the written path, because the arbiter resolves targets against symbol names and has no space for a filesystem path; the written path is kept in metadata.partPath, metadata.partRole is "library" (mandatory on every part_of row), and metadata.isHclIncludePart marks the class. THE WALL, counted rather than hidden: 265 of 287 include sites (92.3 %) carry a COMPUTED path and publish no edge — their targets are discovered by terragrunt at runtime through the directory tree, so a pure AST pass cannot name them; they are refused, not guessed. Falsifier: a corpus `include` block whose `path` is a single string literal that the analyzer publishes no `part_of` edge for, or a `part_of` edge whose target is the written path string rather than a symbol. Pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/terragrunt-include.tf, whose pre-change run is recorded as 12 pass / 1 fail (2 expected part_of edges, 0 actual) and whose post-change run is 13 pass / 0 fail, with forbids for the computed path, the interpolated template (including the template-literal leak), the include with no path, the `terraform_remote_state` data source, `read_terragrunt_config()`, the module block, and the path-shaped target. INSTRUMENT CORRECTION, recorded because a number that changed must say why: a first quick scan classified a path as literal whenever the value contained exactly one string literal, which counted the 257 `find_in_parent_folders("root.hcl")` function-call arguments as literal paths and read 279 literal / 8 computed / 28 present / 251 absent; the committed instrument walks the value structurally (any interpolation, call, variable read, index, arithmetic or conditional marks it computed) and reads 22 literal / 265 computed / 22 present / 0 absent. The 22/265 reading is the one the analyzer and the arm can reproduce; the earlier split was an instrument artifact and is superseded here, not silently replaced.

decisions.node_type: mixes_in — the extended value the lane MEASURED before ruling, on the corpus and against the vocabulary contract
decisions.question: Does HCL have a construct that composes a MEMBER SET from one declaration into another declaration that declares no conformance to it — the shape `mixes_in` asserts?
decisions.resolution: RULED ONTOLOGICAL, after measuring every candidate shape on the CENSUS population (CENSUS (9,329): the lane's own walk — `git ls-files` per checkout under $HOME/fixtures/repositories, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; instrument validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/tools/construct-census.mts + script/m14/hcl-extended-census.ts; parsed=9329/9329 of THAT walk, 16 repositories. THESE ARE CENSUS COUNTS. THE ARM POPULATION IS 11,139 admitted (the gate's own line — script/m14/incoming-gate.ts over root $PWD/.corpus = $HOME/mcp/backbencher-brain/.corpus, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; 38 width-300 slices, contiguous [0, 11,139), CLOSURE EXACT 307,748) and IS the declaration's (validation/m14/instruments/hcl/incoming-declaration.json, derived at HEAD; committed at ba88f2959/e68b41ca7). NO CONSTRUCT COUNT IN THIS SPEC WAS MEASURED ON IT: the two are different populations and a count from one is never quoted as the other's. Artefact validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/extended-census.current.json). THE CONTRACT TEST: `mixes_in` needs a SOURCE declaration whose member set is incorporated, a TARGET declaration that acquires those members as its own, and NO conformance/extends declaration between them (ruby's include/extend/prepend, rust's derive). HCL's candidates each fail one half of that, and the failure is structural rather than incidental: (1) `dynamic` (374 blocks) — the generated block's members are WRITTEN in the source `content` block: 15 dynamic blocks carry nested block children and 359 declare attributes only, so the loop repeats a member set its OWN enclosing declaration writes; the `for_each` expression is a VALUE, never a member-set reference (the 859 for_each sites split 306 identifier reads — var/local values, 263 function calls, 218 conditionals, 41 for-expressions, 28 collection literals, 3 literals). It is a loop-over-a-block, and the block itself declares the members. (2) `for_each` on a resource/module multiplies INSTANCES of one declaration keyed by a value — there is no second declaration on either side. (3) `lifecycle` (227) and `provisioner` (294) blocks are nested members the enclosing resource itself declares; the analyzer already publishes them as `contains`, and a `contains` is not a composition — the parent owns them from the source, it does not acquire them from another declaration. (4) module composition: `module { source }` (2,042) is a separate unit whose members stay namespaced `module.NAME.*` in the caller (the split HCL-D11 measured on the same population), and the `providers` argument (38) binds provider CONFIGURATIONS into that separate unit's slots — the caller's own member set is unchanged, so these are `imports`/`references`. WHY RULED RATHER THAN IMPLEMENTED — THE COMPOSER SIDE WOULD HAVE TO BE INVENTED: to publish a `mixes_in` row on this corpus, the lane would have to designate some variable's value map as the "member set" and some resource block as the "composer", asserting that the variable's entries BECOME the block's members. The tree does not say that: the `content` block writes the generated member shape and the variable only supplies values, and a resource block's members are its own attributes. That designation is a fabrication the vocabulary forbids, and the fleet's rule is that a type is ruled with a class the gate can check rather than published on a guess. Falsifier: a corpus construct in which one declaration's member list is populated by another declaration's members with no conformance/extends declaration between them — e.g. a `dynamic` block whose `content` is not written in the source, a module whose outputs appear in the caller as the caller's own `name.member` addresses, or an attribute that imports another declaration's keys as the target's own members. The ladder was walked: R1 (newer build) and R2 (grammar patch) do not apply — the constructs ARE expressible and are already produced as `block`/`attribute` nodes; the missing half is the composer, which is a semantic fact no grammar can add. R3 (existing node) was the rung used for the MEASUREMENT above; it produces no edge because there is no composer to point at.

decisions.node_type: instantiates — zero-sites closed as IMPLEMENTED + CORPUS-UNEXERCISED
decisions.question: The construct occurs 3,932 times and no bindable type declaration exists anywhere in the corpus. Does the type stay a permanent gap, leave the denominator, or get implemented with a measured unexercised status?
decisions.resolution: IMPLEMENTED AND CORPUS-UNEXERCISED, per the fleet's own class (csharp/rust/matlab precedents; Lead ruling 2026-10-28). RUNG WALK: R1 (newer published grammar build) cannot help — the construct is already expressible and produced as a `block` node with its labels; R2 (grammar patch) is unnecessary for the same reason and would add nothing a resolver could use; R3 (existing node) is the rung taken. THE EMISSION: a `resource` / `data` block publishes `instantiates` from the declaring document's ROOT-MODULE symbol to the PROVIDER TYPE label AS WRITTEN (`aws_instance`; `data "aws_ami"` → `aws_ami`), with metadata.instanceType (the label), metadata.instanceKind (resource|data) and metadata.instanceName (the second label), so a consumer can tell which instance was constructed. The target is symbol-shaped and DELIBERATELY not a declaration the analyzer invents: the provider type is declared by a provider binary, in no repository, so the edge resolves externally or not at all — the contract's own shape for a construction site naming a type the project does not carry. No symbol is created for a provider type (the fixture's forbidSymbols pins that). THE CORPUS-UNEXERCISED `_why`, measured over the CENSUS population (CENSUS (9,329): the lane's own walk — `git ls-files` per checkout under $HOME/fixtures/repositories, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; instrument validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/tools/construct-census.mts + script/m14/hcl-extended-census.ts; parsed=9329/9329 of THAT walk, 16 repositories. THESE ARE CENSUS COUNTS. THE ARM POPULATION IS 11,139 admitted (the gate's own line — script/m14/incoming-gate.ts over root $PWD/.corpus = $HOME/mcp/backbencher-brain/.corpus, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; 38 width-300 slices, contiguous [0, 11,139), CLOSURE EXACT 307,748) and IS the declaration's (validation/m14/instruments/hcl/incoming-declaration.json, derived at HEAD; committed at ba88f2959/e68b41ca7). NO CONSTRUCT COUNT IN THIS SPEC WAS MEASURED ON IT: the two are different populations and a count from one is never quoted as the other's. script/m14/hcl-extended-census.ts, artefact validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/extended-census.current.json): 3,932 resource/data blocks over 444 distinct type labels, and 0 of those labels is a declaration of a TYPE. The 42 address collisions are ALL names that happen to spell a provider type rather than type declarations — 14 variables, 12 modules, 6 outputs, 2 providers, 4 label-less/malformed resource blocks, 1 label-less data block, 3 DSL blocks (http/test/beep) — and 997 of the 3,932 sites carry one of those colliding labels, so the ARM'S `resolved` COLUMN FOR THIS TYPE IS AN UPPER BOUND ON CORRECT TYPE BINDING (production resolution matches by name with no kind filter). DOABILITY: validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/instantiates-resource-type.tf, authored BEFORE the change, pins five positive shapes (two resource kinds and a data source; instanceType/instanceKind/instanceName metadata; the document as source) and nine forbids (lifecycle, dynamic/ingress, the module block and its source path, the variable block, the `list(number)` type expression, the block's full address, and the instance-name label), with forbidsymbols for the provider type; recorded pre-change 13 pass / 1 fail (5 expected rows, 0 actual), post-change 14 pass / 0 fail. Falsifier: a corpus file declaring one of the 444 labels as a TYPE, which would make the relation bindable and move the type out of corpus-unexercised.

decisions.node_type: decorates — the HCL constructs that LOOK like decoration, and why none of them is an applied callable
decisions.question: Does HCL attach an APPLIED CALLABLE to a declaration (the shape `decorates` asserts), or are its decoration-shaped constructs passive metadata?
decisions.resolution: RULED ONTOLOGICAL over the CENSUS population (CENSUS (9,329): the lane's own walk — `git ls-files` per checkout under $HOME/fixtures/repositories, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; instrument validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/tools/construct-census.mts + script/m14/hcl-extended-census.ts; parsed=9329/9329 of THAT walk, 16 repositories. THESE ARE CENSUS COUNTS. THE ARM POPULATION IS 11,139 admitted (the gate's own line — script/m14/incoming-gate.ts over root $PWD/.corpus = $HOME/mcp/backbencher-brain/.corpus, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; 38 width-300 slices, contiguous [0, 11,139), CLOSURE EXACT 307,748) and IS the declaration's (validation/m14/instruments/hcl/incoming-declaration.json, derived at HEAD; committed at ba88f2959/e68b41ca7). NO CONSTRUCT COUNT IN THIS SPEC WAS MEASURED ON IT: the two are different populations and a count from one is never quoted as the other's. Artefact validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/extended-census.current.json). THE MEASURED SURFACE: `validation` blocks 1,228 — assertion blocks attached to a `variable` declaration, and 992 of them invoke a function inside the CONDITION; that call is evaluated by Terraform as an expression at validate/plan time and its RESULT is a boolean, so it is never APPLIED to the declaration. `precondition`/`postcondition` blocks 57 (16 with a call in the condition) are the same fact in lifecycle position. `depends_on` attribute sites 883 carry a list of ADDRESSES and express ORDERING; the analyzer already publishes those reads as `references`, and ordering metadata makes no callable claim. 0 applied-callable candidate sites over the whole population — no construct takes a declaration as the SUBJECT a callable transforms, wraps or annotates. THE LADDER, walked and named: R1 (different/newer published build) is unavailable because the pinned grammar's 64 named node types contain no decorator-shaped production and every published tree-sitter-hcl build is the same container grammar — there is nothing a different build could supply. R2 (patch the grammar) is unavailable in the honest sense: a patch would have to INVENT a syntax the language does not have (no HCL2, terragrunt, packer or nomad dialect has an `@`-shaped or apply-to-declaration form), and inventing syntax is not a grammar remedy. R3 (existing node) is where the MEASUREMENT lives and it yields no edge: the only decoration-shaped nodes are the assertion blocks and `depends_on`, and they are the near misses above. So the relation would assert something the vocabulary does not credit — passive assertion/ordering metadata read as an applied callable — which is the `ontological` class, not a grammar-absence (the nodes exist; the SEMANTICS do not). Falsifier: a corpus construct in which a callable is applied TO a declaration, i.e. the declaration is the subject the callable transforms or annotates — an annotation/decorator on a variable/resource/module declaration, or a call whose receiver is the declaration. The census counts declaration-attached callables (0 today) separately from function calls inside validation conditions (1,008 sites), so the two readings cannot be confused.

decisions.node_type: renders — HCL HAS templates; what it does not have is a declaration the template renders
decisions.question: Does an HCL template render NAME a DECLARATION as its target — the shape `renders` asserts — or does it render a string from text and values?
decisions.resolution: RULED ONTOLOGICAL over the CENSUS population (CENSUS (9,329): the lane's own walk — `git ls-files` per checkout under $HOME/fixtures/repositories, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; instrument validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/tools/construct-census.mts + script/m14/hcl-extended-census.ts; parsed=9329/9329 of THAT walk, 16 repositories. THESE ARE CENSUS COUNTS. THE ARM POPULATION IS 11,139 admitted (the gate's own line — script/m14/incoming-gate.ts over root $PWD/.corpus = $HOME/mcp/backbencher-brain/.corpus, extensions tf,hcl,tfvars,tofu, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB; 38 width-300 slices, contiguous [0, 11,139), CLOSURE EXACT 307,748) and IS the declaration's (validation/m14/instruments/hcl/incoming-declaration.json, derived at HEAD; committed at ba88f2959/e68b41ca7). NO CONSTRUCT COUNT IN THIS SPEC WAS MEASURED ON IT: the two are different populations and a count from one is never quoted as the other's. Artefact validation/m14/fixtures/hcl/extended-census.current.json). THE MEASURED SURFACE: `templatefile()` 60 call sites — and 0 of them has a literal path: all 60 pass a COMPUTED path (`"${path.module}/…"` interpolation), so not one names a file the parse can even see, and 0 names a file inside the admitted population; `templatestring()` 2; `template_dir()` 0; `template_file`/`template_dir` data sources 21, whose rendered output is read as a VALUE (`data.template_file.NAME.rendered`) and is already published as a `references` read; template NODES are abundant — quoted_template 3,710, heredoc_template 3,506 — so the construct is expressible and parsed. WHAT A TEMPLATE DOES HERE: it renders TEXT from text plus values and produces a STRING. There is no construct whose output is a DECLARATION and none that names a declaration as the rendered target: 0 declaration-target candidate sites over the whole population. THE LADDER, walked and named: R1 (different/newer published build) is unavailable because every published tree-sitter-hcl build carries the same template productions, and a newer build would add no declaration-target notion — the missing half is semantic, not syntactic. R2 (patch the grammar) is unavailable honestly: the template nodes already exist, and no HCL2 dialect has a syntax naming a declaration as a render target, so a patch would have to INVENT one. R3 (existing node) is where the measurement lives: the template nodes exist and the analyzer already reads them — interpolated `references` inside `template_interpolation` ARE published, so the data flow is not lost; an edge would need a declaration designated as the rendered target, which the language does not provide. THE CLASS IS ONTOLOGICAL, NOT GRAMMAR-ABSENCE: the grammar HAS template nodes, so a grammar-absence claim would be false; what does not exist is the relation's second half (a declaration target). Falsifier: a corpus construct in which a template render NAMES a declaration as its target — a `templatefile` first argument that is a literal path to an admitted declaration file whose members are rendered into a declaration, or any render construct whose output is a declaration. The extended census counts literal template paths naming admitted files (0) and declaration-target candidates (0).
